CNP Business Flow Gaps
CNP Business Flow Gaps — Three Designs
Three items identified as missing from the seven  core business flows: NDL check (Flow 1),
Annual PY Rollover workflow (Flow 2), and FNS-640/905 reports (Flow 6).
1
NDL Check — National Disqualified List
Flow 1: Sponsor Onboarding & Application
Before a sponsor can be approved to participate in any federal nutrition program, USDA requires
the state agency to verify the applicant is not on the National Disqualified List — a federal
database of individuals and entities permanently barred from USDA food assistance programs
due to fraud, misuse of funds, or serious program violations. An approved sponsor with an
active NDL match is a federal compliance violation.
The NDL check must run at application approval time as a named condition hook on the 
ApproveApplication  workflow transition. If a match is found, the transition is blocked and a
review finding is created requiring the state agency to investigate before approval can proceed.
Integration design
USDA publishes the NDL as a searchable web resource. The platform integrates via the USDA
FNS NDL lookup endpoint, checking three identifying fields: organization name, EIN (Employer
Identification Number), and the names of key principals listed on the application (director,
authorized representative).

Confirmed matches cannot be overriddenA ConfirmedMatch on the NDL is an absolute block
— no override is possible. Only PossibleMatch results can go through the NdlOverrideRequests

Annual Program Year Rollover
Flow 2: Annual Program Year Rollover — pre-populated renewal, checklist, attestation, state
approval
Every July 1, the platform needs to roll every active sponsor's agreements forward into the new
school year. A school district that was approved for NSLP SY2025-26 needs a new agreement
for SY2026-27. Rather than making sponsors start from scratch, the system pre-populates a
renewal with the prior year's data — sites, menus, claim history — and asks the sponsor to
confirm it's still accurate, complete a checklist, and have an authorized director attest to the
information.
This is different from a new application. The data model is the same (SponsorApplications,
ProgramGroupYears) but the workflow is shorter and the initial state is system-generated rather
than user-initiated.

The Hangfire job
A scheduled Hangfire job fires at midnight UTC on October 1 for each active tenant. It is the only
system that creates AutoGenerated renewal records — sponsors cannot initiate a rollover
themselves.

<!-- page: 5 -->
State bulk approvalStates with hundreds of sponsors don't individually review every routine
renewal. The StateReview state supports bulk approval: a state admin can select all renewals
with no changed data, no open compliance findings, and no NDL concerns, and approve them in
a single action. Bulk approval writes individual Approved state transitions for each — the
workflow log shows who approved and when, preserving the audit trail even for bulk operations.
SFSP timing exceptionSFSP sponsors renew on a different cycle — summer program
applications typically open February–April for the coming summer. SFSP rollover uses the same
workflow and tables but fires on a different schedule and generates a SchoolYear of
"Summer2027" rather than "SY2026-27". The IsSFSP flag on the PYRolloverJob row
distinguishes the two cycles.
FNS-640 and FNS-905 Reports
Flow 6: Disbursement of Funds — completing the FNS reporting catalog
The Reporting & Analytics domain currently covers FNS-10, FNS-44, and FNS-418. The spec
also requires FNS-640 (Administrative Review Information) and FNS-905 (Direct Certification
and Verification Summary). Both are annual reports submitted to USDA by each state agency.
FNS-640 — Child Nutrition Programs Administrative Review Information
FNS-640 is the annual summary of compliance review activity. Each state submits it to USDA
showing how many reviews were conducted, what types of findings were identified, how many
fiscal actions were assessed, and how much money was recovered. USDA uses it to evaluate
whether state agencies are meeting their review cycle requirements across all programs.

Rate Availability Constraint
The rollover job (firing ~May 1) and rate insertion are independent operations. Rollover
creates the new ProgramGroupYear and seeds application shells — it does not require
rates to be present. Rates must be inserted into ClaimRateAmounts  separately, before
July 1, when USDA publishes (typically late June). A new PGY with no rates is valid; a claim
submitted against it will fail rate validation until rates exist. Both operations must complete
before claims can be processed for the new school year. Inserting rates before June 30 is
an operational obligation, not just a data entry task.

1 CREATE VIEW analytics.vw_fns640_summary AS
2 SELECT
3 r.TenantCode,
4 r.SchoolYear,
5 r.ProgramCode,
6 COUNT(*) AS ReviewsConducted,
7 COUNT(CASE WHEN r.HasFindings THEN 1 END) AS ReviewsWithFindings,
8 SUM(fa.AmountAssessed) AS TotalFiscalActionAssessed,
9 SUM(rp.AmountRecovered) AS TotalFiscalActionRecovered,
10 COUNT(sd.SerDefId) AS SeriousDeficienciesInitiated
11 FROM analytics.AdminReviews r
12 LEFT JOIN analytics.FiscalActions fa ON fa.ReviewId = r.ReviewId
13 LEFT JOIN analytics.RepaymentSummary rp ON rp.ReviewId = r.ReviewId
14 LEFT JOIN analytics.SeriousDeficiencies sd ON sd.ReviewId = r.ReviewId
15 GROUP BY r.TenantCode, r.SchoolYear, r.ProgramCode

FNS-905 — Direct Certification and Verification Summary
FNS-905 is the annual report on direct certification rates and eligibility verification activity.
States submit it to show USDA how many students were directly certified (automatically, without
household income applications), how many were included in the annual verification sample, and
what the verification outcomes were. USDA uses it to evaluate whether states are meeting
minimum DC rate targets and running compliant verification processes.

Query catalog additions
FNS-640 and FNS-905 both feed the compliance risk scoring AIThe risk scoring model uses
DC match rate as a signal (vw_dc_summary, which feeds FNS-905) and review cycle
compliance as a signal (vw_review_cycles, which feeds FNS-640). Adding these two views to
the reporting catalog means the same data that drives AI-generated risk alerts is also what
populates the federal submissions. One source of truth.
7 COUNT(CASE WHEN d.CertSource = 'Medicaid' THEN 1 END) AS
MedicaidCertifications,
8 COUNT(CASE WHEN d.CertSource = 'TANF' THEN 1 END) AS
TANFCertifications,
9 e.TotalEnrolled,
10 ROUND(COUNT(*) * 100.0 / NULLIF(e.TotalEnrolled, 0), 2) AS
DCRatePct,
11 v.SampleCount AS VerificationSampleSize,
12 v.VerifiedCount,
13 v.ErrorCount,
14 ROUND(v.ErrorCount * 100.0 / NULLIF(v.SampleCount, 0), 2) AS
ErrorRatePct
15 FROM analytics.DirectCertMatches d
16 JOIN analytics.EnrollmentSummary e USING (TenantCode, SchoolYear)
17 LEFT JOIN analytics.VerificationSummary v USING (TenantCode,
SchoolYear)
18 GROUP BY d.TenantCode, d.SchoolYear, e.TotalEnrolled, v.SampleCount,
v.VerifiedCount, v.ErrorCount
